title: Androids, tiled worlds and 240 FPS
summary: The biggest patch yet. The Minoan androids return from painted sheets with rifle, bow and labrys, and Kilon, the pirates and you on foot are redrawn. Planets are built from tile sets in real elevation - forest Amnissos, icy Ida and Kamares, the new volcanic Akrotiri with its four-times-tougher beasts, and the gas giant Dikte's platforms - full of wildlife that grazes, hunts in packs and fights back, with teleport gates and furnished Minoan buildings. Inventories are slots of up to 100, both toolbars have 9 slots you fill, and everything drags and drops; dying loses something you can win back. The sector is renamed after its empires' famous places. And the game now runs at 240 FPS or more everywhere - even on a quad core - with a frame-rate tour and tests that keep it so.

steps.title: The Minoan androids
steps.text: The rigged cut-out characters are gone: sprite sheets draw them better. The Minoan androids return from your painted sheets in 8 views each - one with a laser rifle firing bursts of bolts, one with a laser bow loosing single arrows, one with a double axe (labrys) fighting hand to hand. Kilon Alios, the pirates and you on foot were redrawn from new reference sheets too.

steps.title: Worlds built from tiles
steps.text: Planets are now built from painted isometric tile sets: forest on Amnissos, ice on Ida and Kamares, magma and basalt on Akrotiri, refinery platforms on Dikte. The ground stands up in real elevation - ledges, cliffs, ramps and terraces after a Greek landscape - with one body of water, solid crags you walk round, and back edges you can see. Planets are a quarter of the size (440 x 440 tiles), streamed as you walk.

steps.title: Wildlife, and hunting
steps.text: The planets are alive: over sixty species - goats, deer, wolves and boars, alien beasts and giant insects in the forests, crystal beasts on the ice. Grazers flee, predators hunt in packs and hunt each other, groups defend their own. You can shoot any animal; it leaves Cybernetic Matter; a beast that bites you gets shot back without a click. The Bestiary in the Field Computer records what you've met and hunted.

steps.title: Akrotiri, the volcanic planet
steps.text: A new planet in the home system: Akrotiri, Venus-like - basalt and ash plains, sulphur flats and rivers of magma, painted in the 80s anime style. No one lives there. Its twelve beasts are big and aggressive: four times the health and twice the bite of the creatures they're modelled on, and they drop only minerals.

steps.title: Dikte's platforms, and teleport gates
steps.text: The gas giant Dikte can be landed on now: refinery platforms hovering in its upper clouds, linked by bridges, over a painted cloud deck - industry instead of villages. Every planet has teleport gates: find one and it joins the network, and you can step through to any gate you've discovered, from its own map.

steps.title: Minoan buildings, furnished
steps.text: The Minoan buildings gained a second tile sheet - frescoed and arched walls, statues, fountains, crystal lamps - and their rooms are furnished with painted pieces: tables, thrones, beds, pithoi, looms, altars, consoles, vaults, rugs you walk over. Upper floors have furniture too; containers open once and stay open.

steps.title: Slots, toolbars, drag and drop
steps.text: Inventories are slots now: up to 100 of an item in each. You carry 12 slots on foot; a ship's hold has 12 to 120 by its class. Both toolbars have 9 slots you fill yourself. Drag anything: a stack to another slot, slots to swap, gear onto the toolbar, stacks across at your ship's transfer screen. The Field Computer (Tab) is your menu on foot.

diagram.text: up to 100 of an item per slot  ·  drag to arrange, swap, assign, transfer

steps.title: What you lose, and win back
steps.text: Dying costs something: when your ship is destroyed or you're knocked out on a planet, one thing you carry - a stack or a piece of equipment - is lost. It's never gone for good: every enemy you kill has a 10% chance to win one lost thing back, and 'ITEM REGAINED' tells you what. The list is saved, however many times you die.

steps.title: A sector renamed
steps.text: Every system and its star now bear one of its empire's most famous cities or places - home is Knossos, with Knossos Station - and its planets lesser places of the same empire, every one different: Amnissos (the forest world), Ida, Kamares, Akrotiri, Dikte. Lines, quests and voices were updated.

steps.title: Tools for building it faster
steps.text: Behind the scenes: tests run in parallel (a minute for all of them); live coding - the running game can be inspected, changed and hot-reloaded (LiveLink), debugged with breakpoints, and looked into with Alt + right-click; the Library shows the androids and every building piece; playtests run muted in a corner.

steps.title: From 57 to 240+ FPS
steps.text: A frame-rate tour plays every area for a few seconds in a real window. At first, flying in space ran at 57 FPS and a battle at 25. Engine trails drew hundreds of circles a frame; menus drew the whole world behind them; the ground was thousands of tiles, each texture a separate draw. Now: one atlas for the ground and one for the buildings, the ground drawn as pictures, off-screen things culled and updated less often, decorations redrawn 60 times a second, and nothing heavy in a single frame.

diagram.text: frame rate, before -> now (RTX 2070 Super, 1920 x 1080)

steps.title: Kept at 240, on a quad core too
steps.text: The bar stays: tools/fps_test.py runs the 65-scenario tour and fails anything under 240 FPS, any stutter over 50 ms, or a scenario a quarter slower than its saved baseline; a headless test guards the mechanisms in every test run. Background work takes at most a quarter of the processor, so a quad core plays smoothly too - tested as one.

review.intro: Three days of work: new characters (the Minoan androids, Kilon and the pirates redrawn), tiled planets (forest, ice, volcanic Akrotiri, the gas giant Dikte's platforms) with elevation, wildlife, teleport gates and painted furniture; slot inventories, 9-slot toolbars, drag and drop and lost items; the systems renamed; live-coding tools; and the frame rate - 240 FPS everywhere, on a quad core too, with the tests that keep it.

files.explanation: The notes for Claude: the parallel test runner, and the 240 FPS bar with the tools that keep it.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,8 +1,22 @@ # Space Atrapos - notes for Claude
 # Space Atrapos - notes for Claude
 
-Godot 4.7 game (GDScript). Tests: `godot --headless --path . -s tests/run_tests.gd [-- <file filter>]`
-(back up and restore `~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/Space Atrapos` around test runs).
+Godot 4.7 game (GDScript). Tests: `python3 tools/test.py [<file filter> [<test name filter>]]` - runs them in
+parallel (~1 min for all), each process with its own throwaway user data (no backup needed). One process:
+`godot --headless --path . -s tests/run_tests.gd [-- <file filter> [<test name filter>]]` (back up and restore
+`~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/Space Atrapos` around such runs, or set XDG_DATA_HOME to a scratch folder).
 Talos is the game's editor (title screen > Talos); the docs are data/docs/*.md (F1).
+
+## Frame rate: 240 FPS minimum
+
+The game must run at 240 FPS or more everywhere (the user's bar). `python3 tools/fps_test.py` plays
+every area in a real window (~5 min; `space`, `surface`, `thalassa`... to filter) and fails a scenario
+under 240 FPS (average and 95% of frames), with a frame over 50 ms, or under 3/4 of its baseline
+(tests/fps_baseline.json; `--save-baseline` after a speed-up). Run it after anything that adds per-frame
+work, nodes or drawing; `--profile` shows where the time goes, `--shots` takes screenshots.
+tests/test_frame_budget.gd guards the mechanisms headless (atlases, GroundChunks, far culling, throttled
+redraws, script budgets). Habits that keep it: no draw_circle by the hundred (ExhaustTrail.disc() +
+draw_texture_rect), textures for things drawn together in one atlas (TextureAtlas), cosmetic redraws via
+UI.redraw_due (60 Hz), nothing heavy in one frame (spread it), off-screen things updated less often.
 
 ## Patches: track every change, publish when asked

-# anim | The Animation Editor
-Key-frame animation of the rigged characters: posing parts, keys and interpolation, clips, the timeline, exporting, and how the game plays the clips.
-
-## anim-overview | Animation Editor
-Key-frame animation of the rigged characters (the archer and the guard). Their bodies are cut-out puppets: separate parts hung on a skeleton. The editor animates those parts - moving, rotating, scaling and flipping them frame by frame - on top of the game's built-in motion.
-
-Layout, top to bottom: the **menu bar** (File, Edit, Tools, View, Clip, Key, Help) with the character and view pickers; the [toolbar](doc:anim-toolbar); on the left the [clips](doc:anim-clips) and the [hierarchy](doc:anim-hierarchy); in the centre the [viewport](doc:anim-viewport); on the right the [inspector](doc:anim-inspector); at the bottom the [transport](doc:anim-transport) and the [timeline](doc:anim-timeline).
-
-A typical workflow: pick a **character** and a **view**, pick a **clip** (e.g. `idle`), go to a frame, select a part, pose it with the [tools](doc:anim-tools) (with [Auto-key](doc:anim-keys) on, every change is keyed), go to another frame, pose again, press Space to play. Set the [interpolation](doc:anim-interp) of the keys, then **Save** (Ctrl+S). See [How clips are used in the game](doc:anim-game).
-
-## anim-toolbar | The toolbar
-From left to right:
-- The four [tools](doc:anim-tools): Select (Q), Move (W), Rotate (E), Scale (S).
-- [Flip](doc:anim-flip) horizontally (X) and vertically (Y), and **Reset transform** (Shift+R).
-- [Auto-key](doc:anim-keys) (N) and **Snap** (Shift+S).
-- [Onion skin](doc:anim-onion) (O), and the [view toggles](doc:anim-view): grid (G), bones (B), procedural motion (P), facing left (L).
-- **Fit** (F) at the right end.
-
-## anim-tools | Select, Move, Rotate, Scale
-- **Select (Q)** - click a part to select it; dragging it moves it. **Alt+click** selects the part behind.
-- **Move (W)** - drag the part, or the red / green arrow to move only horizontally / vertically. The offset is measured in the parent's space, so children move along.
-- **Rotate (E)** - drag around the blue ring; the part turns about its joint and its children turn with it.
-- **Scale (S)** - drag the centre square to scale both ways, the red / green handle for width / height. Only the part's own sprite is scaled.
-- **Snap** (Shift+S, or hold Shift while dragging): moves snap to 5 px, rotations to 15°, scales to 0.1.
-- **Reset transform** (Shift+R) puts the part's position, rotation and scale back to the rig's.
-Every drag is one step in Undo (Ctrl+Z).
-
-## anim-flip | Flipping parts
-**Flip horizontally (X)** mirrors the selected part left-right about its joint; **Flip vertically (Y)** turns it upside down about its joint. Both are key-able properties (`Flip H`, `Flip V` in the [inspector](doc:anim-properties)) and **stepped**: they switch exactly at their keys rather than blending. The game draws them too.
-
-## anim-keys | Keys and Auto-key
-A **key** stores a property's value at a frame; between keys the value is [interpolated](doc:anim-interp).
-- **Auto-key (N)** on (red): every edit creates or updates a key at the playhead. Off: edits are only a preview - shown with red key icons - until you key them with **K**; changing frame drops them.
-- **K** keys the selected part (position, rotation, scale and any previewed changes); **Shift+K** keys every part (a full pose); **Alt+K** deletes the part's keys at the playhead.
-- The diamond next to each property in the [inspector](doc:anim-properties) keys just that property. Filled: a key here · outline: keyed elsewhere in the clip · grey: not animated · red: changed, not keyed yet.
-- Copy / paste a pose with Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V (with Shift: the whole pose). In the [timeline](doc:anim-timeline) keys can be selected, dragged, copied and deleted.
-
-## anim-interp | Interpolation and easing
-How values travel from one key to the next, using Godot's Tween transitions:
-- **Constant** holds the value until the next key (a jump).
-- **Linear** moves at an even speed.
-- **Sine, Quad, Cubic, Quart, Quint, Expo, Circ** accelerate progressively more strongly.
-- **Back** overshoots and comes back · **Elastic** springs · **Bounce** bounces · **Spring** settles.
-**Easing** chooses which end is shaped: **In** starts slowly, **Out** ends slowly, **In-Out** both, **Out-In** is fast at both ends and slow in the middle.
-Set them in the [inspector](doc:anim-inspector) for the selected keys (or the part's keys at the playhead), or right-click keys in the [timeline](doc:anim-timeline). New keys take the interpolation of the key before them.
-
-## anim-onion | Onion skin
-Shows the frames before (red) and after (green) the playhead faintly over the character - 1, 2 or 3 of each (O cycles). Use it to judge spacing and arcs.
-
-## anim-view | View options
-- **Grid (G)** - a 25 px grid and the ground line.
-- **Bones (B)** - lines from each part's joint to its parent's; gold joints are animated in this clip.
-- **Procedural motion (P)** - plays the game's built-in motion under the clip (the walk cycle for `walk`, aiming for `attack`, breathing for the others), so you see the final result. Off: only your keys.
-- **Facing left (L)** - shows the character mirrored, as the game draws it walking left.
-- **Fit (F)** frames the character; **Home** resets the view. The wheel zooms at the cursor; middle drag or Space+drag pans. **View > Background** switches dark, light or checker.
-
-## anim-clips | Clips
-Each character and view has its own clips. The game's four:
-- **base** - always applied (permanent adjustments to the rig).
-- **idle** - blends in while standing still (loops at the clip's fps).
-- **walk** - blends in while walking; one loop of the clip is one stride.
-- **attack** - blends in while aiming and shooting; it runs from raising the weapon to the shot.
-Your own clips (New, Ctrl+N) play from code with `RigPuppet.play_clip("name")`. **Duplicate** (Ctrl+D) copies a clip, **Rename** (F2) renames your own, **Delete** (Ctrl+Delete) deletes your own or clears a game clip. The clip's **length**, **fps** and **loop mode** are set in the [inspector](doc:anim-inspector). See [How clips are used in the game](doc:anim-game).
-
-## anim-hierarchy | The hierarchy
-The parts and how they hang together: a child moves and turns with its parent (the forearm with the arm, the head with the torso). Click a part to select it; Tab / Shift+Tab select the next / previous.
-- The **eye** hides the part while you edit (to reach what's behind it) - the game still shows it (H).
-- The **padlock** locks it against clicks in the viewport (Shift+L).
-- ◆ marks parts animated in the current clip.
-
-## anim-viewport | The viewport
-Shows the character at the playhead. Click a part to select it (it's outlined in orange, the part under the cursor in white); drag with the current [tool](doc:anim-tools)'s gizmo. Right-click a part for its menu: key it, delete its keys here, copy / paste its pose, flip it, reset it, hide or lock it.
-
-## anim-inspector | The inspector
-On the right:
-- **Part** - the selected part, its parent, and its Locked / Hidden checkboxes.
-- **Transform** and **Display** - the part's [properties](doc:anim-properties) at the playhead, each with a key button.
-- **Keys** - the [interpolation and easing](doc:anim-interp) of the selected keys, and buttons to key the part, key the pose or delete keys.
-- **Clip** - the clip's length (frames), frames per second, loop mode (loop, ping-pong, play once - as Godot's Animation loop modes) and the preview speed (editor only).
-
-## anim-properties | Part properties
-All are added on top of the rig and the built-in motion:
-- **X, Y** - offset from where the rig puts the part, in rig pixels (children move along).
-- **Rotation** - degrees about the joint (children turn along).
-- **Scale X, Scale Y** - the part's own sprite size (1 = as drawn).
-- **Opacity** - 0 invisible to 1 solid.
-- **Z shift** - moves the part forward (+) or back (-) in the drawing order (stepped).
-- **Flip H, Flip V** - mirrored about the joint ([Flipping](doc:anim-flip), stepped).
-- **Visible** - shows or hides the part in the animation (stepped) - unlike the hierarchy's eye, which only hides it while editing.
-
-## anim-timeline | The timeline
-A row per part; the selected part opens a row per property.
-- **Ruler** - click or drag to move the playhead (red).
-- **Keys** - diamonds (interpolated) or squares (constant / stepped). Click one to select it (Shift / Ctrl: add), drag selected keys to move them in time, drag on empty space to box-select, double-click a property row to add a key there.
-- **Right-click** - delete, copy / paste at the playhead, select all, interpolation and easing.
-- **Keys:** Delete deletes the selected keys · Ctrl+A selects all · Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copy / paste.
-- **Navigation:** Ctrl+wheel zooms the timeline, Shift+wheel scrolls in time, the wheel scrolls the rows. The shaded area is past the clip's end.
-
-## anim-transport | Transport
-Above the timeline: first frame (Shift+Left), previous frame (Left), play / pause (Space), next frame (Right), last frame (Shift+Right), previous / next key (Ctrl+Left / Ctrl+Right), the frame number field, and the time and fps.
-
-## anim-bake | Baking animations | keywords: Bake
-**Bake** (the oven button, Ctrl+B, or Clip > Bake animation) records the current clip exactly as the viewport plays it - the built-in procedural motion (when **Procedural motion** is on) plus your keys, at the clip's length, fps and loop mode - into a fixed frame-by-frame animation, and makes it the game's **default** for the slot you pick:
-- **idle** - standing still · **walk** - walking (one loop of the clip per stride) · **attack** - aiming and shooting · or the clip itself, for one of your own clips.
-In the game, a baked slot plays its recording **instead of** computing the motion: what you saw while baking is what the character does. Baking into another slot copies the clip there first.
-- The clip list marks baked clips **BAKED**. Your keys are kept: editing them removes the bake (the clip goes back to keys + procedural motion) - bake again to update it.
-- **Clip > Remove bake** goes back to keys + procedural motion. Undo (Ctrl+Z) restores a bake too.
-- Each view is baked separately (it has its own parts). Save (Ctrl+S) to keep the bake.
-
-## anim-export | Exporting sprite sheets
-**File > Export** (Ctrl+E) renders the current clip, frame by frame, into a sprite sheet (`data/exports/<character>_<view>_<clip>.png`) and a Godot **SpriteFrames** resource (`.tres`) - put it on an AnimatedSprite2D to play the clip anywhere, without the rig.
-
-## anim-game | How clips are used in the game
-Clips are saved per character in `data/anims/<character>.json`, per view. In the game the character's procedural motion runs (walking, breathing, aiming) and the clips are added on top: `base` always, `idle` while standing, `walk` while walking (one loop per stride), `attack` while aiming (from raising to the shot). Views without clips just use the procedural motion. Your own clips play with `RigPuppet.play_clip("name", loop)`.
-

+# dev-ch | Developer tools
+Looking inside the running game, and changing it while it runs.
+
+## dev-menu | The developer menu and the Inspector | keywords: Alt, inspector, inspect, developer, pause, game speed, hot reload, screenshot
+In a development run of the game (from the project folder - not an exported game), **Alt + right-click** opens the **developer menu**:
+- **Inspect** (the thing under the cursor) - the nearest ship, creature, station or other object of the world there, and **Inspect UI** for the panel or button under the mouse - opens it in the Inspector.
+- **Inspector** - a window inside the game's, along its right edge (drag its title bar to move it, an edge to resize it - an edge brought near the game window's **snaps** flush to it, and stays docked there if the game window changes size; it opens again where you left it; × closes it): the **node tree** of the whole game at the top (type in **Filter nodes...** to find one by name or script; ⟳ Tree rebuilds it), and the selected object's **properties** below - its script's variables first, and with **Built-in** ticked the engine's own (position, scale, modulate...). The values update several times a second as the game runs. Arrays, dictionaries and objects open with their arrow; **double-click** an object to inspect it (**Back** returns to the one before). **Double-click** a number, text, true/false, vector or colour to change it - Enter sets it on the live object. A field that isn't at its **default** (the value its script declares, or the engine's own default) shows a **reset button** (↺) beside its value: click it to put the default back. **Reset all** does it for every field of the object. (A value the game works out as it runs - not written in the script - has no default to go back to, and no button.)
+- **Pause**, **Game speed** (×0.25 to ×4) and **Screenshot** (saved in the game's user folder).
+- **Hot reload** - while ticked, saving a script, shader or picture of the project reloads it in the running game: every object keeps its values and runs the new code from its next frame (variables the new code adds get their declared values). Code that doesn't compile is reported and the old code keeps running. **Buildings** too: change a tile picture (data/sprites/tile_*.png), a Minoan tile sheet in external/images (it's cut into its pieces again by itself) or the building styles (scripts/minoan_tiles.gd - add pieces to a style) and every building on the planet - and the Library's Buildings room - takes the new look at once: same shape, doors and rooms, its walls, floors, roofs, columns and decor redone. (Code that runs once - when an object is created - doesn't run again: re-create the object to see it.)
+
+## live-coding | Live coding with Claude | keywords: live, --live, LiveLink, debugger, breakpoint, step, remote debug, tools/live.py
+Started with `-- --live`, the game also opens a door for **tools/live.py** (on this computer only - port 6070): Claude, or you, can read the game's state (`live.py state`), evaluate expressions (`live.py eval 'ship.hull'`), set values, run whole snippets of GDScript inside the game, hot reload files, take screenshots and follow the log of prints, errors and reloads (`live.py log --follow`) - so a change can be made, tried and tuned while you play, without restarting.
+**The debugger** - start `python3 tools/live.py debugger` first and the game with `--remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:6007`: then breakpoints (`live.py dbg break scripts/hydra_beast.gd 177`), stopping the game, stepping a line at a time (`step`, `next`, `out`, `continue`), the call stack and every variable of a frame (`dbg stack`, `dbg vars`), evaluating expressions where the game stopped, and every error with its call stack (`dbg events`). Script errors don't stop the game unless asked (`dbg errors on`). `python3 tools/live.py help` lists it all.

+- **Wildlife** - forest planets like Amnissos teem with Greek animals: Cretan wild goats, deer and hares (shy - they run when you come close), sheep and pack donkeys grazing round the villages, foxes, tortoises (they pull into their shells), little owls that flit off as you approach, and golden eagles circling overhead - and stranger, alien beasts: striped tigrokeros and glowing selas stags (shy), mushroom mammoths and capped slugs plodding about, bubble toads, moss pangolins that roll into a ball, aeromantas gliding overhead and sky jellies drifting at head height - and giant insects: horned scarabs and rhinoceros beetles, mushroom pillbugs and leaf bugs that roll up into balls, peacock moths, lantern fireflies and dragonflies. Hover over one to see what it is. Animals of one kind stick together: hurt one and **the whole group** near it turns on you - even sheep - while a lone small animal runs. Beware the **predators** (red on the minimap like pirates): **wolf packs** and **harpyx raptor** packs hunt you from afar and close in from all sides, **wild boars** and armoured **hoplorhinos** charge if you come near, and **snakes**, **drakaina serpents**, **giant mantises** - and the insect hunters: **jumping spiders**, **giant centipedes**, **stick mantises**, **fungal stalkers** and **glass grubs** - strike if you step too close. Fight them like pirates (click one, or press F); a badly hurt wolf or harpyx runs. Anything that bites you gets shot back at without a click (you can keep walking - or run), and when the one you were fighting falls you turn on the next that's after you. **Hunting**: any animal can be shot - click it - and every fallen animal leaves a chest of **Cybernetic Matter** (more from the big ones), half flesh, half machine, that stations buy as cargo. Big grazers with horns or antlers (goats, stags, the mushroom mammoth, beetles) turn and fight whoever hurts them; the rest run or hide. The wild has its own food chain too: hungry predators hunt the other animals (anything not bigger than they are), the hunted flee, and predators fight back when attacked. Brought down by an animal, you come to beside your ship - it takes no credits. The **ice planets** (Ida, Kamares) have crystal beasts of their own: shy crystal stags and frost-winged hares, shard crawlers and star crawlers (they curl up), frost rays gliding overhead and ice wisps drifting about - and hunters: **crystal wolf** packs, the charging **frost behemoth**, long-legged **crystal striders**, **frost scuttlers**, **bubble spiders** and **ice wyrms**.
 - Roofs and front walls fade when you're inside or behind them.
 - **Leaving** - click your landed ship or right-click > Leave planet: you return to orbit where you were.
 
+## field-computer | The Field Computer | keywords: Field Computer, Bestiary, Inventory, Medicine, Energy cell, toolbar
+**Tab** opens your Field Computer on a planet - the pilot's own version of the Ship Computer (the game goes on while it's open; it closes by itself if you're attacked). Its tabs (1-5): **Quest** (the main quest's journal), **Inventory** (**I**: your health, rifle and everything you carry - click medicine or an energy cell to use it), **Bestiary** (the planet's wildlife: every creature you've come near, how it behaves, how tough it is and how many you've hunted; the ones you haven't met are silhouettes), **Encyclopedia** and **Map** (the planet map, right in the Field Computer: **M** opens it there).
+
+The **toolbar** at the bottom of the screen has **9 slots** (keys **1-9**, or click) you fill yourself: in the Field Computer's inventory **drag** your rifle, medicine or an energy cell onto a slot (or hover it and press **1-9**); drag slots to swap them; right-click a slot to empty it. Drag the stacks you carry to arrange them. At first: **1 Laser rifle** fires at the nearest enemy (like F); **2 Medicine** heals 50 health (one Medicine from what you carry); **3 Energy cell** overcharges the rifle - twice the rate of fire for 10 s (one Energy Cell, then 20 s before the next). The counts are what you carry - take medicine and cells from your ship's hold at the ship.
+
 ## surface-map | The planet map | keywords: Close the map, Reset view, Layers
-**M** or **Tab** shows the whole planet: you, your ship, every village's buildings and the citizens and pirates near you - in the parts you've explored. **Fog of war**: the planet map and the minimap are dark where you haven't been; walking reveals the land round you (about 44 tiles), and the villages and people there appear. Each planet remembers what you've seen. The wheel zooms (far in: the planet is big), dragging pans, and clicking a spot walks you there - a long way off, you set out toward it and keep going until you arrive. It's drawn like a console's terrain map: glowing cyan coastlines, the land hillshaded, **orange routes** from your ship to each settlement (dotted cyan ones between them), circled icons for the settlements (a temple for the palace), your ship and pirates (red warnings), a compass and a scale bar. The **Layers** panel turns routes, places, people and the grid on and off, and the planet's card sits in the corner.
+**M** shows the whole planet - the Field Computer's Map tab (a teleport gate opens the portal network's own map): you, your ship, every village's buildings and the citizens and pirates near you - in the parts you've explored. **Fog of war**: the planet map and the minimap are dark where you haven't been; walking reveals the land round you (about 44 tiles), and the villages and people there appear. Each planet remembers what you've seen. The wheel zooms (far in: the planet is big), dragging pans, and clicking a spot walks you there - a long way off, you set out toward it and keep going until you arrive. It's drawn like a console's terrain map: glowing cyan coastlines, the land hillshaded, **orange routes** from your ship to each settlement (dotted cyan ones between them), circled icons for the settlements (a temple for the palace), your ship and pirates (red warnings), a compass and a scale bar. The **Layers** panel turns routes, places, people and the grid on and off, and the planet's card sits in the corner.
 
+
+**Teleport gates** - glowing Minoan portal arches stand across every planet: one by the landing pad, one by every village and a few out in the wilds. Click one (walk up to it) and the **portal network** opens - the map with every gate on the planet, linked from the one you're at; click any other gate and you step out in front of it at once.

@@ -1,0 +1,299 @@ 
+"""The Minoan android's animations (build_android.py builds the model and rig)
+and its sprite renders - all at 25 fps, the game's sprite rate.
+
+Clips (each a set of actions, one per animated object, with a fake user;
+AndroidIdle assigned; switch clips with use_clip(name) or in the Action editor):
+  Idle  50 frames (2 s)  breathing, a slow weight shift, glances; rifle at the ready
+  Walk  28 frames        one full cycle in place (two steps: 64 px in 1.1 s in the game)
+  Aim   10 frames        shouldering the rifle (spine turns, head follows the barrel)
+  Fire   6 frames        a shot: muzzle flash, recoil, settling back on aim
+
+Animated: AndroidRig (hips, spine, neck, head), FootIK.L / .R (the legs are IK
+to them), RifleCtrl (the hands are IK to the rifle), MuzzleFlash.
+
+  render_all(out_dir)   every clip frame from 8 directions (the game's camera:
+                        orthographic, 30 degrees above) -> out_dir/<clip><n>_<dir>.png
+                        + meta.json (where the character stands); then
+                        tools/sprites_from_renders.py makes the game's sprites.
+Run: blender -b android.blend --python-expr "import android_anims as a; a.render_all('renders')"
+(with this folder on sys.path), or exec in the open Blender.
+"""
+import json  # noqa
+import math
+import os
+
+import bpy
+from mathutils import Euler, Matrix, Vector
+
+LIFT = 0.13
+FPS = 25
+DIRS = ["e", "se", "s", "sw", "w", "nw", "n", "ne"]
+CLIPS = {"Idle": 50, "Walk": 28, "Aim": 10, "Fire": 6}
+HIP_X, ANKLE_Z = 0.13, 0.15
+
+CARRY = dict(grip=(-0.12, -0.24, 1.12 + LIFT), fwd=(0.55, -0.75, -0.35), up=(0.3, 0.1, 1.0))
+AIM = dict(grip=(-0.07, -0.24, 1.5), fwd=(0.0, -1.0, 0.02), up=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0))
+AIM_TWIST = -0.42     # spine yaw when aiming (the left shoulder comes forward)
+
+
+def _obj(n):
+    return bpy.data.objects.get(n)
+
+
+def _rig():
+    return _obj("AndroidRig")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- posing
+
+def rifle_at(grip, fwd, up=(0, 0, 1)):
+    y = -Vector(fwd).normalized()
+    z = Vector(up).normalized()
+    x = y.cross(z).normalized()
+    z = x.cross(y).normalized()
+    m = Matrix((x, y, z)).transposed().to_4x4()
+    m.translation = Vector(grip)
+    _obj("RifleCtrl").matrix_world = _obj("AndroidRoot").matrix_world @ m
+    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
+
+
+def _lerp_pose(a, b, t):
+    return {k: tuple(Vector(a[k]).lerp(Vector(b[k]), t)) for k in a}
+
+
+def reset():
+    rig = _rig()
+    for pb in rig.pose.bones:
+        pb.location = (0, 0, 0)
+        pb.rotation_euler = (0, 0, 0)
+    for s, sx in (("L", 1), ("R", -1)):
+        _obj("FootIK." + s).location = (HIP_X * sx, 0, ANKLE_Z)
+    fl = _obj("MuzzleFlash")
+    if fl:
+        fl.scale = (0.001, 0.001, 0.001)
+    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
+
+
+def body(drop=0.02, sway=0.0, twist=0.0, lean=0.0, head_yaw=0.0, head_pitch=0.0, breathe=0.0):
+    """The upper body: hips lowered by drop (knees bent a little), swayed /
+    twisted; the spine leans; the head looks."""
+    pb = _rig().pose.bones
+    pb["hips"].location = (0, -drop, 0)              # (bone Y = up)
+    pb["hips"].rotation_euler = (0, sway, 0)          # (about the bone's own axis: a yaw)
+    pb["spine"].rotation_euler = (lean + breathe, twist, 0)
+    pb["neck"].rotation_euler = (-0.5 * lean, -0.4 * twist, 0)
+    pb["head"].rotation_euler = (head_pitch, 0, head_yaw)   # (the head bone points forward: Z is its yaw)
+    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
+
+
+def pose_idle(k, n=CLIPS["Idle"]):
+    reset()
+    t = 2 * math.pi * k / n
+    body(drop=0.02 + 0.004 * math.sin(t), sway=0.03 * math.sin(t), breathe=0.012 * math.sin(2 * t),
+         head_yaw=0.12 * math.sin(t + 0.6), head_pitch=0.03 * math.sin(2 * t))
+    c = dict(CARRY)
+    c["grip"] = tuple(Vector(c["grip"]) + Vector((0, 0, 0.006 * math.sin(2 * t))))
+    rifle_at(**c)
+
+
+DUTY = 0.6
+STEP = 0.40          # m, a foot's travel front to back
+LIFT_H = 0.11        # m, a foot's lift in the swing
+
+
+def _gait(u):
+    """[forward 1..-1, lift 0..1] of a foot at cycle position u (0 = heel strike)."""
+    u %= 1.0
+    if u < DUTY:
+        return 1.0 - 2.0 * u / DUTY, 0.0
+    g = (u - DUTY) / (1.0 - DUTY)
+    e = 0.5 - 0.5 * math.cos(math.pi * g)
+    return -1.0 + 2.0 * e, math.sin(math.pi * g)
+
+
+def pose_walk(k, n=CLIPS["Walk"]):
+    reset()
+    u = k / n
+    for s, sx, off in (("L", 1, 0.0), ("R", -1, 0.5)):
+        fwd, lift = _gait(u + off)
+        _obj("FootIK." + s).location = (HIP_X * sx, -fwd * STEP / 2, ANKLE_Z + lift * LIFT_H)
+    t = 2 * math.pi * u
+    # Hips: lowest just after each heel strike, highest mid-stance; the pelvis
+    # turns with the legs, the chest against it.
+    body(drop=0.06 + 0.025 * math.cos(2 * t), sway=0.12 * math.sin(t), twist=-0.1 * math.sin(t),
+         lean=0.05, head_yaw=0.04 * math.sin(t))
+    c = dict(CARRY)
+    c["grip"] = tuple(Vector(c["grip"]) + Vector((0.01 * math.sin(t), 0, 0.012 * math.cos(2 * t))))
+    rifle_at(**c)
+
+
+def pose_aim(k, n=CLIPS["Aim"]):
+    reset()
+    t = k / (n - 1)
+    e = t * t * (3 - 2 * t)
+    body(drop=0.03, twist=AIM_TWIST * e, lean=0.04 * e, head_yaw=-AIM_TWIST * 0.6 * e, head_pitch=0.08 * e)
+    rifle_at(**_lerp_pose(CARRY, AIM, e))
+
+
+def pose_fire(k, n=CLIPS["Fire"]):
+    reset()
+    kick = [1.0, 0.75, 0.45, 0.22, 0.08, 0.0][min(k, 5)]
+    body(drop=0.03, twist=AIM_TWIST, lean=0.04 - 0.03 * kick, head_yaw=-AIM_TWIST * 0.6, head_pitch=0.08)
+    a = dict(AIM)
+    a["grip"] = tuple(Vector(a["grip"]) + Vector((0, 0.05 * kick, 0.015 * kick)))
+    a["fwd"] = tuple(Vector(a["fwd"]) + Vector((0, 0, 0.12 * kick)))
+    rifle_at(**a)
+    fl = _obj("MuzzleFlash")
+    if fl:
+        s = [1.0, 0.6, 0.001, 0.001, 0.001, 0.001][min(k, 5)]
+        fl.scale = (s, s, s)
+
+
+POSERS = {"Idle": pose_idle, "Walk": pose_walk, "Aim": pose_aim, "Fire": pose_fire}
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the muzzle flash
+
+def make_flash():
+    """A glowing star at the muzzle (on the rifle), shown only when firing."""
+    if _obj("MuzzleFlash"):
+        return
+    import bmesh
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    pts = []
+    for i in range(16):
+        r = 0.16 if i % 2 == 0 else 0.05
+        a = 2 * math.pi * i / 16
+        pts.append(bm.verts.new((r * math.cos(a), 0, r * math.sin(a))))
+    c = bm.verts.new((0, 0, 0))
+    for i in range(16):
+        bm.faces.new((c, pts[i], pts[(i + 1) % 16]))
+    # (and one along the barrel, seen from the side)
+    a1 = bm.verts.new((0, -0.3, 0))
+    a2 = bm.verts.new((0.05, -0.02, 0))
+    a3 = bm.verts.new((-0.05, -0.02, 0))
+    a4 = bm.verts.new((0, -0.02, 0.05))
+    a5 = bm.verts.new((0, -0.02, -0.05))
+    bm.faces.new((a1, a2, a4))
+    bm.faces.new((a1, a4, a3))
+    bm.faces.new((a1, a3, a5))
+    bm.faces.new((a1, a5, a2))
+    me = bpy.data.meshes.new("MuzzleFlash")
+    bm.to_mesh(me)
+    bm.free()
+    me.materials.append(bpy.data.materials["AND_Eye"])
+    ob = bpy.data.objects.new("MuzzleFlash", me)
+    bpy.data.collections["Android"].objects.link(ob)
+    ob.parent = _obj("RifleCtrl")
+    ob.location = (0, -0.63, 0.07)
+    ob.scale = (0.001, 0.001, 0.001)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- actions
+
+ANIMATED = ("AndroidRig", "RifleCtrl", "FootIK.L", "FootIK.R", "MuzzleFlash")
+
+
+def _linear(act):
+    curves = list(getattr(act, "fcurves", []) or [])
+    for layer in getattr(act, "layers", []):
+        for strip in layer.strips:
+            for bag in strip.channelbags:
+                curves += list(bag.fcurves)
+    for fc in curves:
+        for kp in fc.keyframe_points:
+            kp.interpolation = "LINEAR"
+
+
+def bake(clip):
+    """Keyframes clip frames 1..n into actions Android<clip>[<object>]."""
+    n = CLIPS[clip]
+    for name in ANIMATED:
+        ob = _obj(name)
+        ad = ob.animation_data or ob.animation_data_create()
+        ad.action = None
+        old = bpy.data.actions.get(_act_name(clip, name))
+        if old:
+            bpy.data.actions.remove(old)
+    rig = _rig()
+    for k in range(n):
+        f = k + 1
+        POSERS[clip](k, n)
+        for b in ("hips", "spine", "neck", "head"):
+            rig.pose.bones[b].keyframe_insert("location", frame=f)
+            rig.pose.bones[b].keyframe_insert("rotation_euler", frame=f)
+        rc = _obj("RifleCtrl")
+        rc.keyframe_insert("location", frame=f)
+        rc.keyframe_insert("rotation_euler", frame=f)
+        for s in ("L", "R"):
+            _obj("FootIK." + s).keyframe_insert("location", frame=f)
+        _obj("MuzzleFlash").keyframe_insert("scale", frame=f)
+    for name in ANIMATED:
+        ob = _obj(name)
+        act = ob.animation_data.action
+        act.name = _act_name(clip, name)
+        act.use_fake_user = True
+        _linear(act)
+        ob.animation_data.action = None
+
+
+def _act_name(clip, obname):
+    return "Android%s" % clip if obname == "AndroidRig" else "Android%s[%s]" % (clip, obname)
+
+
+def use_clip(clip):
+    """Assigns a clip's actions and sets the scene's frame range to it."""
+    for name in ANIMATED:
+        ob = _obj(name)
+        ob.animation_data.action = bpy.data.actions.get(_act_name(clip, name))
+    sc = bpy.context.scene
+    sc.frame_start, sc.frame_end = 1, CLIPS[clip]
+    sc.render.fps = FPS
+    sc.frame_set(1)
+
+
+def setup_all():
+    make_flash()
+    _obj("RifleCtrl").rotation_mode = "XYZ"
+    for clip in CLIPS:
+        bake(clip)
+    use_clip("Idle")
+    # Timeline markers name the clips' frame ranges when they're laid end to end
+    # in the NLA - here simply the loop length.
+    sc = bpy.context.scene
+    sc.timeline_markers.clear()
+    sc.timeline_markers.new("Idle loop (2 s at 25 fps)", frame=1)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sprites
+
+def facing_angle(d):
+    """AndroidRoot's Z rotation for facing screen direction d (e = right,
+    s = toward the camera): the model faces -Y at 0."""
+    return math.pi / 2 - DIRS.index(d) * math.pi / 4
+
+
+def render_all(out_dir, clips=tuple(CLIPS), dirs=DIRS):
+    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
+    sc = bpy.context.scene
+    root = _obj("AndroidRoot")
+    files = []
+    for clip in clips:
+        use_clip(clip)
+        for k in range(CLIPS[clip]):
+            sc.frame_set(k + 1)
+            for d in dirs:
+                root.rotation_euler = (0, 0, facing_angle(d))
+                bpy.context.view_layer.update()
+                sc.render.filepath = os.path.join(out_dir, "%s%d_%s.png" % (clip.lower(), k + 1, d))
+                bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
+                files.append(sc.render.filepath)
+    root.rotation_euler = (0, 0, 0)
+    from bpy_extras.object_utils import world_to_camera_view
+    uv = world_to_camera_view(sc, sc.camera, root.matrix_world.translation)
+    W = sc.render.resolution_x * sc.render.resolution_percentage // 100
+    H = sc.render.resolution_y * sc.render.resolution_percentage // 100
+    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "meta.json"), "w") as fh:
+        json.dump({"ground": [round(uv.x * W, 2), round((1.0 - uv.y) * H, 2)], "size": [W, H], "fps": FPS}, fh)
+    use_clip("Idle")
+    return files

@@ -1,0 +1,1702 @@ 
+"""Builds the Minoan android (the citizen of data/rigs/android.json; reference:
+external/images/minoan_npc_android.png and minoan_npc_android_parts_*.png) in
+Blender, from scratch, for animated sprites at 25 fps.
+
+  blender -b --python build_android.py                 # builds, saves android.blend + previews
+  (or inside Blender: exec it, then build())
+
+Everything is in the collection "Android", under the empty "AndroidRoot"
+(turn it to face the 8 directions). Facing -Y, feet on z = 0, about 2.2 m to
+the top of the frill. An android: every part is a rigid object parented to
+one bone of "AndroidRig" (no weight painting). The legs are IK chains to the
+foot controls FootIK.L / .R (the feet hang on them, kept flat); the hands are
+IK chains to the rifle (GripR / ForeL on it); the rifle hangs on RifleCtrl
+(child of the chest bone). Animations (25 fps): see android_anims.py.
+
+Look: 1980s anime cel shading - every material is a toon ramp (lit / shade,
+hard edge) on a flat colour, with an ink outline (an inverted hull: a
+Solidify modifier drawing the back faces black). Cream ceramic, bronze-gold
+trim, navy joints, grey-blue ball joints, red cloth, glowing cyan lights; the
+frill, kilt border and cape emblem are painted textures made here (numpy).
+"""
+import math
+import os
+
+import bmesh
+import bpy
+import numpy as np
+from mathutils import Matrix, Vector
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) if "__file__" in globals() else \
+    "/home/kilon/MEGA/Dimitris/godot/space-atrapos/external/blender/android"
+COLL = "Android"
+ROOT = "AndroidRoot"
+RIG = "AndroidRig"
+
+# The skeleton's joints (m; the character's right is -X, it faces -Y).
+ANKLE_Z, KNEE_Z, HIP_Z = 0.15, 0.66, 1.0
+LIFT = 0.13          # the body above the hips is built at HIP_Z = 1.0, then lifted (long legs)
+LEG_HIP = HIP_Z + LIFT
+HIP_X = 0.13
+SHOULDER = Vector((0.30, 0.0, 1.52))
+ELBOW_Z, WRIST_Z = 1.21, 0.93
+NECK_Z = 1.58
+HEAD = Vector((0.0, -0.04, 1.80))
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- palette
+CREAM = (0.93, 0.84, 0.66)
+CREAM_DARK = (0.80, 0.68, 0.50)
+GOLD = (0.95, 0.66, 0.16)
+BRONZE = (0.62, 0.38, 0.12)
+NAVY = (0.16, 0.22, 0.36)
+BALL = (0.47, 0.49, 0.60)
+RED = (0.62, 0.08, 0.07)
+CYAN = (0.25, 0.95, 1.0)
+IVORY = (0.97, 0.93, 0.82)
+GUNMETAL = (0.28, 0.30, 0.34)
+DARK = (0.10, 0.11, 0.14)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- textures
+
+def _image(name, rgb):
+    """A Blender image from an (h, w, 3) float array (top row first)."""
+    h, w = rgb.shape[:2]
+    img = bpy.data.images.get(name)
+    if img and (img.size[0], img.size[1]) != (w, h):
+        bpy.data.images.remove(img)
+        img = None
+    img = img or bpy.data.images.new(name, w, h, alpha=False)
+    px = np.ones((h, w, 4), np.float32)
+    px[:, :, :3] = rgb[::-1]            # (Blender's rows go bottom-up)
+    img.pixels.foreach_set(px.ravel())
+    img.pack()
+    return img
+
+
+def _srgb(c):
+    return np.array(c, np.float32)
+
+
+def _spiral(px, py, cx, cy, r, turns=2.2, width=0.42):
+    """Mask of an Archimedean spiral of radius r centred at (cx, cy)."""
+    dx, dy = px - cx, py - cy
+    rho = np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) / r
+    phi = (np.arctan2(dy, dx) / (2 * math.pi)) % 1.0
+    arm = ((rho * turns - phi) % 1.0) < width
+    return arm & (rho < 1.0) & (rho > 0.08) | (rho <= 0.08)
+
+
+def tex_frill(n=1024):
+    """The frill's painted face (the fan is the lower half of the image, v < 0.5:
+    the plates' -y is up once the frill leans back): cream, bold red petals
+    fanning out from the head, big red spirals round the rim."""
+    y, x = np.mgrid[0:n, 0:n] / (n - 1) * 2.0 - 1.0     # (y down the image = up the fan)
+    out = np.empty((n, n, 3), np.float32)
+    out[:] = _srgb(CREAM)
+    red = np.zeros((n, n), bool)
+    # Petals: long lens shapes fanning out from the head.
+    for k in range(7):
+        ang = math.radians(-160 + k * (140 / 6))
+        u = x * math.cos(ang) - y * math.sin(ang) * -1.0
+        u = x * math.cos(ang) + y * -math.sin(ang) * -1.0
+        cx, cy = math.cos(ang), -math.sin(ang)
+        u = x * cx + y * cy
+        v = -x * cy + y * cx
+        red |= (u > 0.2) & (u < 0.62) & (np.abs(v) < 0.085 * np.sin(np.clip((u - 0.2) / 0.42, 0, 1) * math.pi))
+    # Big spirals round the rim.
+    for k in range(7):
+        ang = math.radians(-205 + k * (230 / 6))
+        cx, cy = 0.74 * math.cos(ang), -0.74 * math.sin(ang)
+        red |= _spiral(x, y, cx, cy, 0.19, turns=2.1, width=0.36)
+    out[red] = _srgb(RED)
+    r = np.sqrt(x * x + y * y)
+    out[(r > 0.9) & (r < 0.94)] = _srgb(CREAM_DARK)     # (a band inside the rim)
+    return out
+
+
+def tex_band(w=1024, h=256):
+    """The kilt's cloth: cream, a red border with a cream running wave near
+    the hem, a thin red stripe above it."""
+    v, u = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w] / np.array([h - 1, w - 1])[:, None, None]
+    v = 1.0 - v                      # 0 = hem, 1 = belt
+    out = np.empty((h, w, 3), np.float32)
+    out[:] = _srgb(CREAM)
+    out[((u * 32.0) % 1.0) < 0.5] = _srgb(tuple(c * 0.93 for c in CREAM))   # (the pleats' shaded halves)
+    band = (v > 0.04) & (v < 0.26)
+    out[band] = _srgb(RED)
+    t = (v - 0.04) / 0.22
+    x = u * 18.0
+    wave = np.abs(t - (0.5 + 0.28 * np.sin(2 * math.pi * x))) < 0.13
+    curl = _spiral(x % 1.0, t, 0.25, 0.42, 0.22, turns=1.5, width=0.45)
+    out[band & (wave | curl)] = _srgb(CREAM)
+    out[(v > 0.30) & (v < 0.32)] = _srgb(RED)
+    out[v < 0.02] = _srgb(CREAM_DARK)
+    return out
+
+
+def tex_belt(w=1024, h=128):
+    """The belt: gold with a row of bronze chevrons (u round the waist)."""
+    v, u = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w] / np.array([h - 1, w - 1])[:, None, None]
+    out = np.empty((h, w, 3), np.float32)
+    out[:] = _srgb(GOLD)
+    x = (u * 28.0) % 1.0
+    y = np.abs(v - 0.5) * 2.0                     # 0 at the middle, 1 at the edges
+    chev = (np.abs(x - 0.5 - 0.25 * y) < 0.09) & (y < 0.6)
+    out[chev] = _srgb(BRONZE)
+    out[(v < 0.1) | (v > 0.9)] = _srgb(BRONZE)
+    return out
+
+
+def tex_wave(w=1024, h=128):
+    """A red Minoan band with a cream running wave and gold edges (cuffs)."""
+    v, u = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w] / np.array([h - 1, w - 1])[:, None, None]
+    out = np.empty((h, w, 3), np.float32)
+    out[:] = _srgb(RED)
+    x = u * 10.0
+    t = (v - 0.12) / 0.76
+    wave = (t > 0) & (t < 1) & (np.abs(t - (0.5 + 0.28 * np.sin(2 * math.pi * x))) < 0.14)
+    curl = _spiral(x % 1.0, t, 0.3, 0.45, 0.26, turns=1.5, width=0.45) & (t > 0) & (t < 1)
+    out[wave | curl] = _srgb(CREAM)
+    out[(v < 0.1) | (v > 0.9)] = _srgb(GOLD)
+    return out
+
+
+def tex_cape(n=1024):
+    """The cape: red, a gold border band on the hem and sides, a gold
+    triskelion in the middle of the back (u: around, v: down from the top)."""
+    v, u = np.mgrid[0:n, 0:n] / (n - 1)
+    out = np.empty((n, n, 3), np.float32)
+    out[:] = _srgb(RED)
+    border = (v > 0.92) | (u < 0.035) | (u > 0.965)
+    out[border] = _srgb(GOLD)
+    # Triskelion: three spirals round a centre.
+    cx, cy, R = 0.5, 0.38, 0.17
+    gold = np.zeros((n, n), bool)
+    for k in range(3):
+        ang = math.radians(90 + k * 120)
+        sx, sy = cx + 0.55 * R * math.cos(ang), cy - 0.55 * R * math.sin(ang)
+        gold |= _spiral(u, v, sx, sy, 0.55 * R, turns=1.6, width=0.4)
+    gold |= np.hypot(u - cx, v - cy) < 0.018
+    out[gold] = _srgb(GOLD)
+    return out
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- materials
+
+def _new_mat(name):
+    m = bpy.data.materials.get(name) or bpy.data.materials.new(name)
+    m.use_nodes = True
+    nt = m.node_tree
+    nt.nodes.clear()
+    return m, nt
+
+
+def _lin(c):
+    """sRGB (as painted) -> the linear values Blender's colour inputs take."""
+    return tuple(x / 12.92 if x <= 0.04045 else ((x + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4 for x in c)
+
+
+def mat_toon(name, color, shade=0.58, image=None, mapping=None, hi=0.0):
+    """Cel shading: diffuse light -> two hard tones (lit, shade) times the
+    colour (or a painted image); a thin bright rim on the lit edge."""
+    m, nt = _new_mat(name)
+    out = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputMaterial")
+    out.location = (900, 0)
+    dif = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfDiffuse")
+    dif.location = (-400, 200)
+    dif.inputs["Color"].default_value = (1, 1, 1, 1)
+    s2r = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeShaderToRGB")
+    s2r.location = (-200, 200)
+    nt.links.new(dif.outputs[0], s2r.inputs[0])
+    bw = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeRGBToBW")
+    bw.location = (0, 200)
+    nt.links.new(s2r.outputs["Color"], bw.inputs[0])
+    ramp = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
+    ramp.location = (150, 200)
+    ramp.color_ramp.interpolation = "CONSTANT"
+    els = ramp.color_ramp.elements
+    sh = _lin((shade, shade * 0.95, min(1.0, shade * 1.05)))
+    els[0].position, els[0].color = 0.0, (*sh, 1)
+    els[1].position, els[1].color = 0.42, (1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1)
+    if hi > 0:       # (a third tone: the anime highlight where the light hits square)
+        e = els.new(0.86)
+        e.color = (1.0 + hi, 1.0 + hi, 1.0 + hi * 0.9, 1)
+    nt.links.new(bw.outputs[0], ramp.inputs["Fac"])
+    if image is not None:
+        tx = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
+        tx.location = (-200, -150)
+        tx.image = image
+        tx.interpolation = "Closest" if image.size[0] < 300 else "Linear"
+        col = tx.outputs["Color"]
+    else:
+        rgb = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeRGB")
+        rgb.location = (-200, -150)
+        rgb.outputs[0].default_value = (*_lin(color), 1)
+        col = rgb.outputs[0]
+    mul = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeMix")
+    mul.data_type = "RGBA"
+    mul.blend_type = "MULTIPLY"
+    mul.location = (450, 100)
+    mul.inputs["Factor"].default_value = 1.0
+    nt.links.new(col, mul.inputs[6])
+    nt.links.new(ramp.outputs["Color"], mul.inputs[7])
+    em = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeEmission")
+    em.location = (680, 0)
+    nt.links.new(mul.outputs[2], em.inputs["Color"])
+    nt.links.new(em.outputs[0], out.inputs["Surface"])
+    return m
+
+
+def mat_glow(name, color, strength=2.2):
+    m, nt = _new_mat(name)
+    out = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputMaterial")
+    em = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeEmission")
+    em.inputs["Color"].default_value = (*_lin(color), 1)
+    em.inputs["Strength"].default_value = strength
+    nt.links.new(em.outputs[0], out.inputs["Surface"])
+    return m
+
+
+def mat_outline(name="AND_Ink", color=(0.006, 0.004, 0.005)):
+    m, nt = _new_mat(name)
+    out = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputMaterial")
+    em = nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeEmission")
+    em.inputs["Color"].default_value = (*color, 1)
+    nt.links.new(em.outputs[0], out.inputs["Surface"])
+    m.use_backface_culling = True
+    return m
+
+
+M = {}
+INK = 2.7          # outline thickness multiplier (the sprites are small: bold ink)
+
+
+def make_materials():
+    M.update({
+        "cream": mat_toon("AND_Cream", CREAM, hi=0.07),
+        "cream_dark": mat_toon("AND_CreamDark", CREAM_DARK, hi=0.07),
+        "gold": mat_toon("AND_Gold", GOLD, shade=0.5, hi=0.3),
+        "bronze": mat_toon("AND_Bronze", BRONZE, shade=0.55, hi=0.2),
+        "belt": mat_toon("AND_Belt", GOLD, shade=0.5, hi=0.3, image=_image("AND_belt", tex_belt())),
+        "wave": mat_toon("AND_Wave", RED, shade=0.6, image=_image("AND_wave", tex_wave())),
+        "navy": mat_toon("AND_Navy", NAVY, shade=0.6),
+        "ball": mat_toon("AND_Ball", BALL, shade=0.6),
+        "red": mat_toon("AND_Red", RED, shade=0.6, hi=0.08),
+        "ivory": mat_toon("AND_Ivory", IVORY, shade=0.66, hi=0.1),
+        "gunmetal": mat_toon("AND_Gunmetal", GUNMETAL, shade=0.6),
+        "steel": mat_toon("AND_Steel", (0.56, 0.58, 0.63), shade=0.55, hi=0.25),
+        "dark": mat_toon("AND_Dark", DARK, shade=0.7),
+        "cyan": mat_glow("AND_Cyan", CYAN, 2.4),
+        "eye": mat_glow("AND_Eye", (0.55, 1.0, 1.0), 3.0),
+        "ink": mat_outline(),
+        "frill": mat_toon("AND_Frill", CREAM, image=_image("AND_frill", tex_frill())),
+        "kilt": mat_toon("AND_Kilt", CREAM, image=_image("AND_kilt", tex_band())),
+        "cape": mat_toon("AND_Cape", RED, shade=0.6, image=_image("AND_cape", tex_cape())),
+    })
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- mesh helpers
+
+def _coll():
+    c = bpy.data.collections.get(COLL)
+    if c is None:
+        c = bpy.data.collections.new(COLL)
+        bpy.context.scene.collection.children.link(c)
+    return c
+
+
+def _obj(name):
+    return bpy.data.objects.get(name)
+
+
+def _link(name, data):
+    ob = bpy.data.objects.new(name, data)
+    _coll().objects.link(ob)
+    return ob
+
+
+def mesh_object(name, bm, mats, smooth=False, outline=0.006, bevel=0.0):
+    me = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
+    bm.to_mesh(me)
+    bm.free()
+    for p in me.polygons:
+        p.use_smooth = smooth
+    ob = _link(name, me)
+    for m in mats:
+        me.materials.append(M[m])
+    if bevel > 0:
+        b = ob.modifiers.new("Bevel", "BEVEL")
+        b.width, b.segments, b.limit_method = bevel, 2, "ANGLE"
+    outline *= INK
+    if outline > 0:
+        me.materials.append(M["ink"])
+        s = ob.modifiers.new("Ink", "SOLIDIFY")
+        s.thickness = -outline        # (outward from the surface)
+        s.offset = -1.0
+        s.use_flip_normals = True
+        s.use_rim = False
+        s.material_offset = len(me.materials) - 1
+    return ob
+
+
+def _orient(bm, verts, p1, p2):
+    """Moves verts made along +Z (0..1 long) to run from p1 to p2."""
+    p1, p2 = Vector(p1), Vector(p2)
+    d = p2 - p1
+    q = Vector((0, 0, 1)).rotation_difference(d.normalized())
+    bmesh.ops.transform(bm, matrix=Matrix.Translation(p1) @ q.to_matrix().to_4x4() @ Matrix.Diagonal((1, 1, d.length, 1)), verts=verts)
+
+
+def limb(name, p1, p2, r1, r2, mat="cream", seg=14, squash=(1.0, 1.0), smooth=True, outline=0.006):
+    """A tapered cylinder from p1 to p2 (radius r1 -> r2), capped."""
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    res = bmesh.ops.create_cone(bm, cap_ends=True, segments=seg, radius1=r1, radius2=r2, depth=1.0)
+    bmesh.ops.translate(bm, vec=(0, 0, 0.5), verts=res["verts"])
+    bmesh.ops.scale(bm, vec=(squash[0], squash[1], 1), verts=res["verts"])
+    _orient(bm, res["verts"], p1, p2)
+    return mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=smooth, outline=outline)
+
+
+def ball(name, loc, r, mat="ball", scale=(1, 1, 1), seg=16, outline=0.005, half=False, rot=(0, 0, 0)):
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    bmesh.ops.create_uvsphere(bm, u_segments=seg, v_segments=seg // 2, radius=r)
+    if half:
+        bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=[v for v in bm.verts if v.co.z < -1e-4], context="VERTS")
+    bmesh.ops.scale(bm, vec=scale, verts=bm.verts)
+    if rot != (0, 0, 0):
+        bmesh.ops.transform(bm, matrix=_euler(rot).to_matrix().to_4x4(), verts=bm.verts)
+    bmesh.ops.translate(bm, vec=loc, verts=bm.verts)
+    return mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=True, outline=outline)
+
+
+def box(name, size, loc, mat="cream", rot=(0, 0, 0), taper=None, bevel=0.01, outline=0.006):
+    """A box (size x, y, z) at loc; taper = (top x scale, top y scale)."""
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    bmesh.ops.create_cube(bm, size=1.0)
+    for v in bm.verts:
+        if taper and v.co.z > 0:
+            v.co.x *= taper[0]
+            v.co.y *= taper[1]
+        v.co.x *= size[0]
+        v.co.y *= size[1]
+        v.co.z *= size[2]
+    bmesh.ops.transform(bm, matrix=Matrix.LocRotScale(Vector(loc), Matrix.Rotation(0, 3, "Z").to_quaternion() if rot == (0, 0, 0) else
+                                                      _euler(rot), None), verts=bm.verts)
+    return mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], bevel=bevel, outline=outline)
+
+
+def _euler(rot):
+    from mathutils import Euler
+    return Euler(rot, "XYZ").to_quaternion()
+
+
+def torus(name, loc, R, r, mat="gold", normal=(0, 0, 1), seg=32, outline=0.004):
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    verts = []
+    for i in range(seg):
+        a = 2 * math.pi * i / seg
+        for j in range(8):
+            b = 2 * math.pi * j / 8
+            verts.append(bm.verts.new(((R + r * math.cos(b)) * math.cos(a), (R + r * math.cos(b)) * math.sin(a), r * math.sin(b))))
+    for i in range(seg):
+        for j in range(8):
+            a, b = i * 8 + j, i * 8 + (j + 1) % 8
+            c, d = ((i + 1) % seg) * 8 + (j + 1) % 8, ((i + 1) % seg) * 8 + j
+            bm.faces.new((verts[a], verts[b], verts[c], verts[d]))
+    q = Vector((0, 0, 1)).rotation_difference(Vector(normal).normalized())
+    bmesh.ops.transform(bm, matrix=Matrix.Translation(loc) @ q.to_matrix().to_4x4(), verts=bm.verts)
+    return mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=True, outline=outline)
+
+
+def cone(name, base, tip, r, mat="ivory", seg=12, outline=0.005, curve=0.0, side=None):
+    """A horn / claw: a cone from base to tip, optionally curved toward side."""
+    base, tip = Vector(base), Vector(tip)
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    rings = 6
+    side = Vector(side or (0, 0, 1)).normalized()
+    rows = []
+    for k in range(rings + 1):
+        t = k / rings
+        c = base.lerp(tip, t) + side * curve * math.sin(math.pi * t) * (base - tip).length
+        rr = r * (1 - t) + 0.002
+        d = (tip - base).normalized()
+        q = Vector((0, 0, 1)).rotation_difference(d)
+        row = []
+        for i in range(seg):
+            a = 2 * math.pi * i / seg
+            row.append(bm.verts.new(c + q @ Vector((rr * math.cos(a), rr * math.sin(a), 0))))
+        rows.append(row)
+    for k in range(rings):
+        for i in range(seg):
+            bm.faces.new((rows[k][i], rows[k][(i + 1) % seg], rows[k + 1][(i + 1) % seg], rows[k + 1][i]))
+    bm.faces.new(rows[0][::-1])
+    bm.faces.new(rows[-1])
+    return mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=True, outline=outline)
+

+def sheet(name, fn, nu, nv, mat, thick=0.012, outline=0.005, uv=True):
+    """A cloth sheet: fn(u, v) -> point, u, v in 0..1, given thickness."""
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    uvl = bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
+    grid = [[bm.verts.new(fn(i / nu, j / nv)) for i in range(nu + 1)] for j in range(nv + 1)]
+    for j in range(nv):
+        for i in range(nu):
+            f = bm.faces.new((grid[j][i], grid[j][i + 1], grid[j + 1][i + 1], grid[j + 1][i]))
+            for loop, (a, b) in zip(f.loops, ((i, j), (i + 1, j), (i + 1, j + 1), (i, j + 1))):
+                loop[uvl].uv = (a / nu, 1.0 - b / nv)
+    ob = mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=True, outline=outline)
+    if thick:
+        s = ob.modifiers.new("Thick", "SOLIDIFY")
+        s.thickness = thick
+        ob.modifiers.move(len(ob.modifiers) - 1, 0)
+    return ob

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- shaped helpers (v2)

+def _se(a, b, n, seg, th0=0.0, th1=2 * math.pi, closed=True):
+    """Points of a superellipse (half-sizes a, b; n = 2 round .. 6 boxy);
+    angle 0 = +b (the front), going round toward +a."""
+    out = []
+    count = seg if closed else seg + 1
+    for i in range(count):
+        t = th0 + (th1 - th0) * i / seg
+        s, c = math.sin(t), math.cos(t)
+        out.append((a * math.copysign(abs(s) ** (2.0 / n), s), b * math.copysign(abs(c) ** (2.0 / n), c)))
+    return out
+
+
+def _frame_to(p1, p2, front=(0, -1, 0)):
+    """A matrix taking local z (0..1 = p1..p2 in metres), local y = front,
+    x = y cross z... to the world."""
+    p1, p2 = Vector(p1), Vector(p2)
+    z = (p2 - p1).normalized()
+    f = Vector(front)
+    y = (f - z * f.dot(z))
+    if y.length < 1e-6:
+        y = Vector((0, -1, 0)) - z * z.y * -1
+    y.normalize()
+    x = y.cross(z)
+    m = Matrix((x, y, z)).transposed().to_4x4()
+    m.translation = p1
+    return m
+
+
+def _flat_caps(ob, n):
+    """The last n faces (a loft's caps) shaded flat."""
+    ps = ob.data.polygons
+    for i in range(len(ps) - n, len(ps)):
+        if i >= 0:
+            ps[i].use_smooth = False
+
+
+def loft(name, secs, mat="cream", axis="z", seg=24, outline=0.006, bevel=0.0, frame=None, smooth=True, round_ends=True):
+    """A lofted solid through rounded cross-sections secs = [(t, c1, c2, a, b, n)].
+    axis "z": rings at z = t centred (x=c1, y=c2), half-sizes a (x), b (y);
+    axis "y": rings at y = t centred (x=c1, z=c2), a (x), b (z).
+    frame: a matrix applied after (limb space: local z along the limb)."""
+    if round_ends and len(secs) >= 2:
+        # (rounded ends: a smaller ring a little beyond each end, so the flat
+        # caps are small and the ends read as rounded plates, not cut blocks)
+        def _end(p, q):
+            t, c1, c2, a, b, n = p
+            d = math.copysign(min(a, b) * 0.3, p[0] - q[0])
+            return (t + d, c1, c2, a * 0.7, b * 0.7, n)
+        secs = [_end(secs[0], secs[1])] + list(secs) + [_end(secs[-1], secs[-2])]
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    uvl = bm.loops.layers.uv.new("UVMap")
+    rings = []
+    for (t, c1, c2, a, b, n) in secs:
+        ring = []
+        for (u, w) in _se(a, b, n, seg):
+            co = (c1 + u, c2 + w, t) if axis == "z" else (c1 + u, t, c2 + w)
+            ring.append(bm.verts.new(co))
+        rings.append(ring)
+    t0, t1 = secs[0][0], secs[-1][0]
+    for k in range(len(rings) - 1):
+        v0 = (secs[k][0] - t0) / (t1 - t0) if t1 != t0 else 0.0
+        v1 = (secs[k + 1][0] - t0) / (t1 - t0) if t1 != t0 else 1.0
+        for i in range(seg):
+            j = (i + 1) % seg
+            f = bm.faces.new((rings[k][i], rings[k][j], rings[k + 1][j], rings[k + 1][i]))
+            for loop, (uu, vv) in zip(f.loops, ((i / seg, v0), ((i + 1) / seg, v0), ((i + 1) / seg, v1), (i / seg, v1))):
+                loop[uvl].uv = (uu, 1.0 - vv)
+    bm.faces.new(rings[0][::-1])
+    bm.faces.new(rings[-1])
+    bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=bm.faces)
+    if frame is not None:
+        bmesh.ops.transform(bm, matrix=frame, verts=bm.verts)
+    ob = mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=smooth, outline=outline, bevel=bevel)
+    _flat_caps(ob, 2)
+    return ob
+
+
+def limb_loft(name, p1, p2, secs, mat="cream", front=(0, -1, 0), seg=24, outline=0.006):
+    """A loft along a limb from p1 to p2: secs = [(f, dx, dy, a, b, n)] with
+    f = 0..1 along it, dy toward `front`."""
+    L = (Vector(p2) - Vector(p1)).length
+    return loft(name, [(f * L, dx, dy, a, b, n) for (f, dx, dy, a, b, n) in secs], mat, "z", seg,
+                outline=outline, frame=_frame_to(p1, p2, front))
+
+
+def shell(name, p1, p2, secs, th0, th1, thick=0.018, mat="cream", front=(0, -1, 0), seg=24, outline=0.005):
+    """An armour plate wrapping a limb: the part of the rounded section between
+    angles th0..th1 (radians, 0 = front, + toward local +x), from f0 to f1
+    along p1 -> p2; secs = [(f, a, b, n)] (outer half-sizes)."""
+    L = (Vector(p2) - Vector(p1)).length
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    outer, inner = [], []
+    for (f, a, b, n) in secs:
+        o = [bm.verts.new((u, w, f * L)) for (u, w) in _se(a, b, n, seg, th0, th1, closed=False)]
+        i = [bm.verts.new((u, w, f * L)) for (u, w) in _se(a - thick, b - thick, n, seg, th0, th1, closed=False)]
+        outer.append(o)
+        inner.append(i)
+    for k in range(len(secs) - 1):
+        for j in range(seg):
+            bm.faces.new((outer[k][j], outer[k][j + 1], outer[k + 1][j + 1], outer[k + 1][j]))
+            bm.faces.new((inner[k][j + 1], inner[k][j], inner[k + 1][j], inner[k + 1][j + 1]))
+        for j in (0, seg):   # (the side edges)
+            bm.faces.new((outer[k][j], outer[k + 1][j], inner[k + 1][j], inner[k][j]))
+    for k in (0, len(secs) - 1):   # (the ends)
+        for j in range(seg):
+            bm.faces.new((outer[k][j], inner[k][j], inner[k][j + 1], outer[k][j + 1]))
+    bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=bm.faces)
+    bmesh.ops.transform(bm, matrix=_frame_to(p1, p2, front), verts=bm.verts)
+    return mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=True, outline=outline)
+

+def tube(name, pts, r, mat="dark", seg=10, ribs=0.0, outline=0.004, steps=6):
+    """A hose along points pts (smoothed), radius r; ribs = rib spacing (m)."""
+    P = [Vector(p) for p in pts]
+    path = []
+    for i in range(len(P) - 1):           # Catmull-Rom through the points
+        p0, p1, p2, p3 = P[max(i - 1, 0)], P[i], P[i + 1], P[min(i + 2, len(P) - 1)]
+        for s in range(steps):
+            t = s / steps
+            path.append(0.5 * ((2 * p1) + (-p0 + p2) * t + (2 * p0 - 5 * p1 + 4 * p2 - p3) * t * t + (-p0 + 3 * p1 - 3 * p2 + p3) * t ** 3))
+    path.append(P[-1])
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    rings = []
+    dist = 0.0
+    nrm = None
+    for k, p in enumerate(path):
+        d = (path[min(k + 1, len(path) - 1)] - path[max(k - 1, 0)]).normalized()
+        if nrm is None:
+            nrm = d.orthogonal().normalized()
+        nrm = (nrm - d * nrm.dot(d)).normalized()
+        bin_ = d.cross(nrm)
+        if k:
+            dist += (p - path[k - 1]).length
+        rr = r * (1.0 + (0.22 if ribs and (dist / ribs) % 1.0 < 0.45 else 0.0))
+        rings.append([bm.verts.new(p + (nrm * math.cos(2 * math.pi * i / seg) + bin_ * math.sin(2 * math.pi * i / seg)) * rr) for i in range(seg)])
+    for k in range(len(rings) - 1):
+        for i in range(seg):
+            j = (i + 1) % seg
+            bm.faces.new((rings[k][i], rings[k][j], rings[k + 1][j], rings[k + 1][i]))
+    bm.faces.new(rings[0][::-1])
+    bm.faces.new(rings[-1])
+    bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=bm.faces)
+    ob = mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=True, outline=outline)
+    _flat_caps(ob, 2)
+    return ob
+
+
+def _se_pt(a, b, n, th):
+    s, c = math.sin(th), math.cos(th)
+    return (a * math.copysign(abs(s) ** (2.0 / n), s), b * math.copysign(abs(c) ** (2.0 / n), c))
+
+
+def _interp(secs, t):
+    """The section at t, linearly between the given ones (by their first value)."""
+    secs = sorted(secs, key=lambda q: q[0])
+    if t <= secs[0][0]:
+        return secs[0]
+    if t >= secs[-1][0]:
+        return secs[-1]
+    for p, q in zip(secs, secs[1:]):
+        if p[0] <= t <= q[0]:
+            k = (t - p[0]) / (q[0] - p[0]) if q[0] != p[0] else 0.0
+            return tuple(x + (y - x) * k for x, y in zip(p, q))
+    return secs[-1]
+
+
+def on_limb(p1, p2, secs, th, f, front=(0, -1, 0), lift=0.004):
+    """A point on a limb_loft's / shell's surface (angle th, fraction f),
+    lifted a little off it (for lines and trim laid on the plate)."""
+    L = (Vector(p2) - Vector(p1)).length
+    v = _interp(secs, f)
+    if len(v) == 4:
+        _, a, b, n = v
+        dx = dy = 0.0
+    else:
+        _, dx, dy, a, b, n = v
+    u, w = _se_pt(a + lift, b + lift, n, th)
+    return _frame_to(p1, p2, front) @ Vector((dx + u, dy + w, f * L))
+
+
+def on_loft(secs, axis, th, t, lift=0.004):
+    """A point on a loft's surface (angle th, at t along its axis)."""
+    _, c1, c2, a, b, n = _interp(secs, t)
+    u, w = _se_pt(a + lift, b + lift, n, th)
+    return Vector((c1 + u, c2 + w, t)) if axis == "z" else Vector((c1 + u, t, c2 + w))

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the head (traced)
+# The skull is traced from the reference board's head panel: head/ref_head.png
+# (external/images/minoan_npc_android.png, crop (560,385)-(960,705), scaled x2;
+# head/ref_grid.png has the grid). Every outline below is in that picture's
+# pixels (x forward, y down); HP() puts them on the model. The parts are flat-
+# faceted plates (straight edges, flat shading), so their ink outlines draw the
+# panel lines as the painting does.
+K_V = 0.00101                  # m per reference pixel
+REF_YAW, REF_EL = math.radians(64), math.radians(8)   # the panel's view: turned 64 degrees, 8 above
+
+
+def HP(px, py, x=0.0):
+    """A reference pixel -> (y, z) on the head (before LIFT), for a point at
+    lateral x (the near side is -x): in the panel's 3/4 view a point's sideways
+    offset moves it on the picture too, so it's undone here (head/overlay.py
+    renders the same view to check)."""
+    st, ct = math.sin(REF_YAW), math.cos(REF_YAW)
+    f = ((px - 300) * K_V - x * ct) / st
+    dY = x * st - f * ct
+    dz = ((300 - py) * K_V - dY * math.sin(REF_EL)) / math.cos(REF_EL)
+    return (HEAD.y - f, HEAD.z + dz)
+
+
+def near(px, py, w_fn, it=2):
+    """(x, y, z) of a near-side point traced at (px, py), at w_fn(pc, py) off
+    the centre line (pc: the centre-line pixel of the same forward position)."""
+    pc = px
+    for _ in range(it):
+        x = -w_fn(pc, py)
+        y, z = HP(px, py, x)
+        pc = 300 + (HEAD.y - y) * math.sin(REF_YAW) / K_V
+    return (x, y, z)

+    return out
+
+
+def skull_xm(f, z):
+    """The core's half-width at forward f, height z (model space)."""
+    _, zt, zb, hw, wt, wb = _interp(_skull_m(), f)
+    ct, cb = CH_TOP * K_V, CH_BOT * K_V
+    if z >= zt:
+        return wt
+    if z > zt - ct:
+        return wt + (hw - wt) * (zt - z) / ct
+    if z >= zb + cb:
+        return hw
+    if z > zb:
+        return wb + (hw - wb) * (z - zb) / cb
+    return wb
+
+
+def on_skull(px, py, base=0.0, it=4):
+    """(x, y, z) of the near-side point drawn at reference pixel (px, py) on
+    the skull's surface (base off it)."""
+    x = -(skull_x(px, py) + base)
+    for _ in range(it):
+        y, z = HP(px, py, x)
+        x = -(skull_xm(HEAD.y - y, z) + base)
+    y, z = HP(px, py, x)
+    return (x, y, z)
+
+
+def skull_sec(px):
+    return _interp([tuple(float(v) for v in q) for q in SKULL], px)
+
+
+def skull_x(px, py):
+    """The skull's half-width at reference pixel (px, py) (clamped to its outline)."""
+    _, top, bot, hw, ft, fb = skull_sec(px)
+    if py <= top:
+        return ft * hw
+    if py < top + CH_TOP:
+        return hw * (ft + (1 - ft) * (py - top) / CH_TOP)
+    if py <= bot - CH_BOT:
+        return hw
+    if py < bot:
+        return hw * (1 - (1 - fb) * (py - (bot - CH_BOT)) / CH_BOT)
+    return fb * hw
+
+
+def _mesh_from(name, rings_or_none, verts, faces, mat, outline, bevel, smooth=False):
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    vs = [bm.verts.new(v) for v in verts]
+    caps = []
+    for f in faces:
+        try:
+            face = bm.faces.new([vs[i] for i in f])
+            if len(f) > 4:
+                caps.append(face)
+        except ValueError:
+            pass
+    if caps:
+        bmesh.ops.triangulate(bm, faces=caps, quad_method="BEAUTY", ngon_method="EAR_CLIP")
+    bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=bm.faces)
+    ob = mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=smooth, outline=outline)
+    if bevel > 0:
+        b = ob.modifiers.new("Bevel", "BEVEL")
+        b.width, b.segments, b.limit_method, b.angle_limit = bevel, 1, "ANGLE", math.radians(40)
+        ob.modifiers.move(len(ob.modifiers) - 1, 0)
+    return ob
+
+
+def skull_core(name="Skull"):
+    """The skull: an octagonal section at each SKULL station, joined by flat faces."""
+    verts, faces = [], []
+    n = 8
+    ct, cb = CH_TOP * K_V, CH_BOT * K_V
+    for (f, zt, zb, hw, wt, wb) in _skull_m():
+        y = HEAD.y - f
+        for (x, z) in ((wt, zt), (hw, zt - ct), (hw, zb + cb), (wb, zb),
+                       (-wb, zb), (-hw, zb + cb), (-hw, zt - ct), (-wt, zt)):
+            verts.append((x, y, z))
+    for k in range(len(SKULL) - 1):
+        for i in range(n):
+            j = (i + 1) % n
+            faces.append((k * n + i, k * n + j, (k + 1) * n + j, (k + 1) * n + i))
+    faces.append(tuple(range(n))[::-1])
+    last = (len(SKULL) - 1) * n
+    faces.append(tuple(range(last, last + n)))
+    ob = _mesh_from(name, None, verts, faces, "cream", 0.005, 0.0)
+    ob.modifiers.new("Tri", "TRIANGULATE").min_vertices = 4   # (as the plates see it)
+    ob.modifiers.move(len(ob.modifiers) - 1, 0)
+    return ob
+
+
+def inset(pts, g):
+    """A polygon (reference px) shrunk by g px all round (each edge moved in)."""
+    n = len(pts)
+    area = sum(pts[i][0] * pts[(i + 1) % n][1] - pts[(i + 1) % n][0] * pts[i][1] for i in range(n))
+    sgn = 1.0 if area > 0 else -1.0
+    out = []
+    for i in range(n):
+        p0, p1, p2 = Vector(pts[i - 1]), Vector(pts[i]), Vector(pts[(i + 1) % n])
+        e0, e1 = (p1 - p0).normalized(), (p2 - p1).normalized()
+        n0 = Vector((-e0.y, e0.x)) * sgn
+        n1 = Vector((-e1.y, e1.x)) * sgn
+        m = (n0 + n1)
+        if m.length < 1e-6:
+            m = n0
+        m.normalize()
+        k = g / max(0.35, m.dot(n0))
+        q = p1 + m * k
+        out.append((q.x, q.y))
+    return out
+

+def panel(name, pts, sx, mat="cream", thick=0.013, base=0.0, gap=4.0, bone="head"):
+    """A plate with a panel line all round it: a dark backing of the full outline
+    under the plate, inset gap px (the painting's ink seams between plates)."""
+    part(side_plate(name + "Seam", pts, sx, "dark", thick=0.003, base=0.0008, bevel=0.0, outline=0.0, cuts=10), bone)
+    return part(side_plate(name, inset(pts, gap), sx, mat, thick=thick, base=0.0028 + base, bevel=0.0, outline=0.0, cuts=10), bone)

+def side_plate(name, pts, sx, mat="cream", thick=0.014, base=-0.004, bevel=0.003, outline=0.004, cuts=6):
+    """A plate on the skull's side, outline pts traced (reference px): the
+    outline is subdivided in the picture's pixels and every vertex put on the
+    skull's surface (skull_x - the same shape the core is built from), so the
+    plate follows its facets and chamfers; then it's given its thickness
+    outward. base: its offset off the skull (stack plates with it)."""
+    bm = bmesh.new()
+    f = bm.faces.new([bm.verts.new((px, py, 0.0)) for (px, py) in pts])
+    bmesh.ops.triangulate(bm, faces=[f], quad_method="BEAUTY", ngon_method="EAR_CLIP")
+    bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges(bm, edges=bm.edges[:], cuts=cuts, use_grid_fill=True)
+    for v in bm.verts:
+        px, py = v.co.x, v.co.y
+        x, y, z = on_skull(px, py, base)
+        v.co = (-sx * x, y, z)
+    bm.normal_update()
+    zmid = HEAD.z - 0.05
+    flip = [fc for fc in bm.faces if fc.normal.dot(Vector((fc.calc_center_median().x, 0, fc.calc_center_median().z - zmid))) < 0]
+    bmesh.ops.reverse_faces(bm, faces=flip)            # (every face facing out of the skull)
+    ob = mesh_object(name, bm, [mat], smooth=False, outline=0.0)
+    so = ob.modifiers.new("Thick", "SOLIDIFY")
+    so.thickness = thick
+    so.offset = 1.0
+    if bevel > 0:
+        bv = ob.modifiers.new("Bevel", "BEVEL")
+        bv.width, bv.segments, bv.limit_method, bv.angle_limit = bevel, 1, "ANGLE", math.radians(50)
+    if outline * INK > 0:
+        ob.data.materials.append(M["ink"])
+        ink = ob.modifiers.new("Ink", "SOLIDIFY")
+        ink.thickness = -outline * INK
+        ink.offset = -1.0
+        ink.use_flip_normals = True
+        ink.use_rim = False
+        ink.material_offset = len(ob.data.materials) - 1

+def profile_solid(name, pts, hw, mat="ivory", bevel=0.004, outline=0.005):
+    """A solid from a side outline (reference px), across the head: half-width
+    hw(px, py) at each outline point (tapering shapes - the beak, the jaw)."""
+    verts = []
+    for (px, py) in pts:
+        x, y, z = near(px, py, hw)
+        w = -x
+        verts.append((w, y, z))
+        verts.append((-w, y, z))
+    n = len(pts)
+    faces = [tuple(2 * i for i in range(n)), tuple(2 * i + 1 for i in range(n))[::-1]]
+    for i in range(n):
+        j = (i + 1) % n
+        faces.append((2 * i, 2 * i + 1, 2 * j + 1, 2 * j))
+    return _mesh_from(name, None, verts, faces, mat, outline, bevel)
+
+
+def _smooth(P, steps=4):
+    P = [Vector(p) for p in P]
+    out = []
+    for i in range(len(P) - 1):
+        p0, p1, p2, p3 = P[max(i - 1, 0)], P[i], P[i + 1], P[min(i + 2, len(P) - 1)]
+        for s in range(steps):
+            t = s / steps
+            out.append(0.5 * ((2 * p1) + (-p0 + p2) * t + (2 * p0 - 5 * p1 + 4 * p2 - p3) * t * t + (-p0 + 3 * p1 - 3 * p2 + p3) * t ** 3))
+    out.append(P[-1])
+    return out
+
+
+def ribbon(name, pts, sx, width, thick, mat="gold", outline=0.004):
+    """A flat band along pts (3D), lying against the skull's side (normal +-x)."""
+    pts = _smooth(pts)
+    out = Vector((sx, 0, 0))
+    verts, faces = [], []
+    for k, p in enumerate(pts):
+        t = (pts[min(k + 1, len(pts) - 1)] - pts[max(k - 1, 0)]).normalized()
+        up = t.cross(out).normalized()
+        for (a, b) in ((-1, -1), (1, -1), (1, 1), (-1, 1)):
+            verts.append(tuple(p + up * (a * width / 2) + out * (b * thick / 2)))
+    m = len(pts)
+    for k in range(m - 1):
+        for i in range(4):
+            j = (i + 1) % 4
+            faces.append((4 * k + i, 4 * k + j, 4 * (k + 1) + j, 4 * (k + 1) + i))
+    faces.append((3, 2, 1, 0))
+    faces.append((4 * (m - 1), 4 * (m - 1) + 1, 4 * (m - 1) + 2, 4 * (m - 1) + 3))
+    return _mesh_from(name, None, verts, faces, mat, outline, 0.0, smooth=False)
+

+def at_side(px, py, sx, off=0.0):
+    """A point on the skull's side at reference pixel (px, py), off it by off."""
+    x, y, z = on_skull(px, py, off)
+    return Vector((-sx * x, y, z))

+    root = _empty(ROOT, (0, 0, 0), size=0.4, shape="CIRCLE")

+    for name, bone in PARTS.items():

+            # The feet hang on their IK controls (kept flat on the ground).
+            mw = ob.matrix_world.copy()
+            ob.parent = _obj("FootIK." + bone.split(".")[1])
+            ob.matrix_world = mw
+        else:

+        ob.matrix_basis = mw

+    _empty("GripR", (0, 0.0, -0.02), rc, 0.03)
+    _empty("ForeL", (0, -0.27, -0.03), rc, 0.03)

+def rifle_at(grip, fwd, up=(0, 0, 1)):
+    """Puts the rifle (RifleCtrl) with its grip at `grip` (world, the
+    character at rest facing -Y), the muzzle along fwd, its top toward up."""
+    y = -Vector(fwd).normalized()
+    z = Vector(up).normalized()
+    x = y.cross(z).normalized()
+    z = x.cross(y).normalized()
+    m = Matrix((x, y, z)).transposed().to_4x4()
+    m.translation = Vector(grip)
+    rc = _obj("RifleCtrl")
+    rc.matrix_world = _obj(ROOT).matrix_world @ m
+    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
